key_insight: The paper finds that the main bottleneck in object-goal navigation is not exploration, but goal grounding: agents often fail to recognize when the target is already visible or how close it is. The proposed StopWatch approach targets this missing capability directly, rather than only improving navigation behavior.
problem_solved: It addresses the low success rate of VLM-based object-goal navigation policies by diagnosing and fixing their inability to ground the goal in the current observation, especially for in-view detection and distance estimation.
method: Diagnose navigation failures to identify goal grounding as the dominant weakness in fine-tuned VLM policies.
Introduce a method called StopWatch that focuses the policy on recognizing whether the goal is already visible and estimating proximity.
Use this grounding-aware capability to improve decision-making during navigation instead of relying on exploration alone.
impact: For AI/ML practitioners, this work shows that stronger pretrained models still need explicit grounding skills for embodied tasks. It suggests that improving perception of goal presence and distance can unlock larger gains than simply scaling navigation policies.

paper_title: StopWatch: Goal Grounding for Object-goal Navigation
paper_authors: Xinhao Liu, Yunsheng Tian, Yuheng Qiu, Pieter Abbeel, Xi Chen
